The All Progressives Congress in Yobe State has distributed 500 empowerment items to youths and women in Zone B Senatorial District as part of efforts to strengthen grassroots support ahead of the 2027 general elections. The distribution, which took place during a solidarity rally in Fika Local Government Area on Sunday, featured motorcycles, tricycles, popularly known as Jega, and sewing machines. The exercise was carried out by the party’s governorship candidate, Baba Wali, on behalf of Governor Mai Mala Buni, as part of the state government’s efforts to improve livelihoods and promote economic empowerment among residents. The rally also marked the commencement of the APC’s grassroots mobilisation campaign in the state, with the party seeking support for President Bola Tinubu, Wali and other candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Addressing party supporters, Wali expressed confidence in the APC’s chances, dismissing the possibility of opposition parties defeating the ruling party in the state. Highlighting some of the achievements of the Buni administration, Wali listed road construction, the Gadaka Road, Galda Market and Gadaka General Hospital among projects executed by the state government. He also appealed to residents to support the completion of ongoing projects, particularly those involving potable water supply and other development initiatives across the state. The governorship candidate described his ambition as one of continuity, promising to sustain the development programmes of the current administration if elected. He also cited the Nafada–Potiskum highway as one of the federal infrastructure projects being undertaken under the Tinubu administration. The rally attracted APC stakeholders, youths, women and other supporters from across Zone B. Also speaking, Bomai, who represents the senatorial district, urged residents to support Tinubu, Wali and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. The state APC Chairman, Muhammadu Gadaka, said the party would extend the mobilisation exercise to the remaining senatorial districts as part of efforts to consolidate its support base across the state’s 17 local government areas.
